title: A compact generative language model learns sequence grammar associated with protein phase separation
summary: A compact, task-specific generative model trained on 137 curated protein sequences reproduced length-dependent sequence-property patterns and generated candidate peptides. Four of five synthesized 20–25-residue peptides showed droplet-like and turbidity signatures at 1 mM in buffer. These observations are preliminary: only five short peptides were tested, one had reduced purity, and liquid-state behavior was not confirmed by FRAP or reversibility assays; functional condensates were not established.
ai_technology: A roughly 17-million-parameter generative language model trained from scratch on a curated set of phase-separating and folded proteins generated candidate sequences for testing.
organization: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Hyderabad; Washington University in St. Louis

evidence.tested: The model reproduced sequence-property trends and generated candidates; four of five short synthesized candidates showed condensation signatures in microscopy and turbidity assays. Simulations of 89 longer sequences were computational evidence, not experimental validation.
evidence.unknown: The small peptide sample and millimolar test concentration limit generalization. Definitive liquid behavior and functional condensate activity were not established.
evidence.ai_role: A roughly 17-million-parameter generative language model trained from scratch on a curated set of phase-separating and folded proteins generated candidate sequences for testing.
